- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 18d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates; adjust upward by 3–8% if supply net < -15 and sentiment < 0.33.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); forecast should be closer to 18d moving average if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- When official events are sparse (e.g., <5 events/30d), model overfits to recent history; reduce forecast volatility by 15–25% to avoid overreaction to noise.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint (e.g., if sentiment shifts from 0.67 to 0.00, forecast should drop 5–10% immediately).
